title: Financial Literacy & Credit Management for Farmer Members
description: Educational guide on Kisan Credit Card (KCC), prompt repayment interest subvention, and debt management for rural cooperative members.
content:
Financial literacy enables farmers and cooperative members to make informed decisions regarding credit, savings, insurance, and investment.

Key Financial Literacy Principles:
1. Kisan Credit Card (KCC):
   - KCC provides farmers with flexible, hassle-free short-term credit for crop production and post-harvest maintenance.
   - Interest Subvention Scheme: The Central Government provides interest subvention on short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3 Lakhs, offering additional subvention for prompt repayment, effectively reducing the net interest rate.
2. Prompt Repayment Benefit:
   - Timely repayment of crop loans before the due date maintains a healthy credit history (CIBIL score) and qualifies the farmer for interest subvention discounts.
   - Defaulting leads to penalty interest, loss of subvention benefits, and restriction on fresh credit facility.
3. Avoiding Informal High-Interest Loans:
   - Members should prioritize borrowing from institutional sources like PACS, District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), and commercial banks rather than informal moneylenders who charge exorbitant interest rates.
4. Budgeting and Savings:
   - Regularly setting aside a portion of harvest proceeds into recurring or fixed deposits in cooperative banks ensures financial security during lean seasons.
